metadata.title: Data Density Pass 16 -- Day 3 Cannonade Preparation and Bombardment (Ticks 505-540)
metadata.description: Alexander's artillery line deployment, the two-hour Confederate cannonade (largest artillery bombardment in American history to that point), Union counterbattery and Osborn's Cemetery Hill guns, the Confederate ceasing fire, and Pickett's division stepping off. Individual battery placements with Alexander's ammunition anxiety note.

placements.notes: Alexander positioning his 75-gun line. He will command the Confederate cannonade.
Washington Artillery of New Orleans -- 9 guns
Dearing's battalion -- 20 guns
Henry's battalion -- 20 guns
Cabell's battalion -- 18 guns
Pegram's battalion on the northern flank of the Confederate line
McIntosh's battalion -- Whitworth rifles included
Osborn's Cemetery Hill batteries -- 40 guns. Will answer the Confederate cannonade.
McGilvery's Plum Run Line -- 39 guns on Cemetery Ridge south
Cushing's Battery A at The Angle -- 6 guns
Brown's Battery B, 1st RI -- 6 guns on Cemetery Ridge
CANNONADE BEGINS at 1 PM. Alexander fires the signal guns. Confederate bombardment opens.
Washington Artillery firing -- the largest artillery bombardment in American history
Dearing's guns opening -- overshooting the Union line
Pegram's guns -- also overshooting, striking the Taneytown Road behind Cemetery Hill
Osborn answering with full force -- later ordered to reduce fire to deceive Alexander
McGilvery's guns returning fire -- 160 Union guns total engaged
Cushing's battery firing -- two of Cushing's guns already disabled
Alexander's ammunition running low. Sends Pickett the famous note: For God's sake come quick.
McGilvery ordered to stop firing -- deceiving Alexander into thinking the Union guns are beaten
Osborn's guns going silent -- the deception is working
Cushing still firing -- 4 of his 6 guns now out of action. Two remain.
Garnett stepping off. The charge begins.
Kemper stepping off.
Armistead stepping off last, behind Garnett and Kemper.
